corrections.reason: Failed to recognize that when a Solver echoes back format instructions instead of producing content, this indicates unclear task specification from the Coordinator (B.1). The error manifests in the Solver's output but originates from the Coordinator's ambiguous instructions.

Alpha incorrectly assigned B.1 (Coordinator_Unclear_Task_Specification). This error is not about the coordinator's task specification being unclear - it's about the solver completely failing to execute any task at all, instead outputting system prompts and templates. B.1 would only apply if the coordinator's instructions were ambiguous and that caused confusion; here the solver didn't even attempt to follow instructions of any kind.

Confused the symptom (output lacking task execution) with causation. A.8 applies when the agent PERFORMS its task but fails to package output correctly for downstream consumers. Here, the agent never performed the task because it didn't receive proper instructions - this is an upstream issue (A.7), not downstream handoff failure.

B.2 is about solver's analytical failure to assess evidence gaps in their reasoning process. The error here is operational - the retrieval chain wasn't executed at all. The agent is 'solver' but the error is about retrieval operations not being performed, which is a coordinator function that failed to happen. Alpha focused on 'solver' as the agent but missed that the actual error is about the multi-hop retrieval chain termination.

Alpha chose B.2 (Solver_Insufficient_Evidence_Analysis) which applies when a solver analyzes evidence but fails to identify gaps. However, the error states NO retrieval was performed at all in a task requiring exactly three hops. This is not about insufficient evidence analysis - it's about the coordinator failing to execute the required multi-hop retrieval chain. The distinguishing rule states: 'Coordinator stops hop sequence = B.9'. Since the coordinator stopped at 0/3 hops, this is clearly B.9.

Misidentified this as a downstream formatting issue when the agent actually refused to perform the task entirely. The agent didn't fail to structure output properly - it failed to produce any substantive output at all.

Alpha confused the symptom (lack of proper output structure) with the root cause. A.8 (Downstream_Handoff_Failure) applies when an agent completes its task but fails to format output properly for the next component. Here, the agent never attempted the task at all - it just returned the template. The missing information isn't a handoff formatting issue; it's because no work was performed.
